gen-gf-gabarito-gf-martel: Gabarito draws every curve as if with a single nib, its cut-open terminals letting the counters flow outward. Martel, a text serif, swells gently in its rounds and reads easily underneath.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-mate: Gabarito looks drawn with one nib, its strokes showing no difference between upright and sideways, and its terminals cut open. Mate, a text serif, has cupped round letters and a soft step from heavy to light, so long paragraphs would feel dignified and unhurried.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-mate-sc: Expressive open-ended curves in Gabarito, all traced at a single pressure, sit above a body with more nuance in it. Mate SC lets its classic serif curves taper like lifted brush strokes, which keeps a long page gentle.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-nanum-myeongjo: Nanum Myeongjo reads quietly, a text serif whose curve tips never touch and whose strokes ebb and flow. Gabarito then adds its hairline-free, one-nib heading, so the page moves from a drawn voice into a refined one.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-noto-serif-hk: Distinctive is the right word for Gabarito, whose strokes have no brush-style swell and whose terminals are cut open. Noto Serif HK, a classic serif, brings a middle-of-the-road contrast and thinner crossbars, giving the headline an editorial partner that stays dignified.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-noto-serif-jp: Gabarito looks drawn with a single pen tip, its terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. Noto Serif JP, a text serif, is the better one for sustained reading, with curves a little heavier than its joins.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-noto-serif-kr: Gabarito gives even its w a single stroke thickness, with terminals cut open and counters flowing outward. It earns its keep big and short, while Noto Serif KR does the quiet work.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-noto-serif-sc: Gabarito keeps horizontals and verticals identical in thickness, like rod stock, with its terminals cut open. Noto Serif SC, a text serif, then thickens its round letters slightly at the sides and gives the page a literary, medium-contrast texture.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-noto-serif-tc: Refined letters in Noto Serif TC hold their shapes open, stems barely heavier than the arms that join them, while Gabarito feels like tracing one thick thread. Its hairlines are neither wispy nor heavy, so a long stretch reads steadily.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-petrona: Gabarito does its best work big and short, a one-nib heading in which a t has crossbar and stem at one width. Petrona, a classic serif, keeps a mid-range gap between its boldest and faintest strokes.
